purpose: Predeclared, uncontaminated 8-case fresh pilot for the intent-revised Cerebras gpt-oss-120b candidate. Written and committed to disk BEFORE any new inference call under the frozen revision (nlu_cerebras_intent_revision_frozen.json). All gold labels below are copied verbatim from evaluation/v2/nlu_benchmark_v1.json's dev split; none were altered.
benchmark_source: evaluation/v2/nlu_benchmark_v1.json 'dev' split (45 examples) ONLY. The 105-example 'test' split (consumed once, pre-closure) and any Phase-10 held-out data are NOT touched.
case_selection_rationale: Covers the same 8 semantic-surface categories as the prior pilot (nlu_cerebras_gptoss_pilot_plan.json) but with 8 DIFFERENT query_ids, 8 different query texts, and 8 different template_group instances (verified programmatically - see overlap_verification below). At least one A_literature_evidence example is included (nlu_v1_0002). Two non-A cases were deliberately chosen because their surface form contains literature/evidence-flavored language alongside a more specific structural requirement - exactly the shape that could plausibly be misclassified as generic A: nlu_v1_0091 (E_multi_hop_research, ends '...and what published efficacy evidence exists?') and nlu_v1_0140 (I_ambiguous, 'What's new in cancer research?' - a bare-topic research question). Neither of these two, nor any other case, reuses the wording, entities, or template_group of the two questions that failed in the prior pilot (nlu_v1_0100, nlu_v1_0136).
known_limitation: As in the prior pilot, no example in the 45-item dev split is a true 'ambiguous ABBREVIATION' case (an acronym with 2+ biomedical meanings). The closest available I_ambiguous dev example not already used in the prior pilot, nlu_v1_0140 ('What's new in cancer research?' - a bare, unscoped research question with no target/disease/population), is substituted for that slot; disclosed here rather than silently reinterpreted.

pilot_cases.query_text: What does published research say about KRAS inhibition in melanoma?
Find active, not recruiting Phase 3 trials in elderly patients with Alzheimer's disease using HER2 inhibitors

pilot_cases.category: multi-entity question (also: A-confusable, literature-flavored trailing clause)
pilot_cases.query_text: Which compounds targeting EGFR have entered trials for non-small cell lung cancer, and what published efficacy evidence exists?
Which drugs have both ChEMBL bioactivity data and clinical trial records for melanoma?

pilot_cases.category: ambiguous-abbreviation (substituted - see known_limitation; also: A-confusable, bare research-topic mention)
pilot_cases.note: Benchmark lists required_sources=['pubmed'] as the template's nominal downstream source, but intent_class is I_ambiguous and adjudication_notes confirms this is a genuinely underspecified query (no target/disease/population) - scored on intent==I_ambiguous and ambiguity.is_ambiguous==true, consistent with how nlu_v1_0136 was scored in the prior pilot.

pilot_cases.query_text: By what biochemical pathway does adagrasib inhibit mTOR signaling?
pilot_cases.note: mTOR is a canonical gene/protein/target ambiguity case for this benchmark's semantic_roles field, same role BTK played in the prior pilot's case 0071; gold benchmark itself has no gold semantic_roles annotation (documented pre-existing limitation), so this case is scored on entity_type/normalization correctness plus qualitative semantic_roles behavior, not a semantic_roles P/R/F1 number.

pilot_cases.query_text: What Phase 3 trials are evaluating sotorasib in type 2 diabetes?
Find recruiting Phase 1 trials in adults with multiple myeloma using JAK2 inhibitors

overlap_verification.method: Programmatic check (venv/bin/python, ad hoc script, not persisted as project code - one-off verification) comparing query_id, exact query_text, and template_group of all 8 new cases against the prior pilot's 8 cases and the full 105-example consumed test split.
overlap_verification.result: PASS - zero overlap on every dimension checked. Some cases share a template FAMILY prefix with the prior pilot (e.g. tmplG appears in both, tmplE/tmplE2, tmplD/tmplD2, tmplA/tmplA2, tmplF/tmplF3) with different substituted parameters (different target/disease/compound/constraint values) - this is expected (the dev split only has a finite number of template families) and does not constitute example reuse; template_group (the full parameter-instantiated string) is disjoint in all 8 cases.

request_settings_predeclared.response_format: strict json_schema (CEREBRAS_RESEARCH_QUERY_JSON_SCHEMA, nlu/extractor.py - unchanged from prior pilot)
request_settings_predeclared.prompt: nlu/extractor.py::CEREBRAS_INTENT_CLARIFIED_PROMPT (the ONE frozen revision - see nlu_cerebras_intent_revision_frozen.json). Identical to the prior pilot's STRUCTURED_EXTRACTION_PROMPT plus exactly one added RULES bullet.
request_settings_predeclared.retry_policy: 1 initial attempt + 1 identical retry on empty/unparseable/malformed response only, matching every other candidate's empty_response_handling contract
request_settings_predeclared.rate_limiting: sequential calls only, throttled via utils.rate_limiter (5 RPM Free Trial cap), no parallel/burst requests

hard_rejection_gate_reminder: Reject immediately (no full dev run) on any SYSTEMIC defect: generic-intent collapse, repeated B/G confusion, catastrophic entity loss, repeated entity mistyping, fabricated canonical IDs, major constraint loss, broad false ambiguity, semantic_roles regression, semantically-empty-but-valid outputs, normalization corruption, repeated unsupported field invention. Target for intent: 8/8 correct. One isolated minor error does not automatically disqualify (classify per Step 14-15's (A)/(B)/(C) test); a clear systemic pattern does. There is no second revision regardless of outcome.
latency_gate_reminder: Control: P50 19150ms / P95 66983ms (artifacts/v2/nlu_frozen_config.json). True (throttle-excluded) latency must show >=60% P50 AND >=60% P95 reduction; ideally P50<=5s/P95<=15s. Throttle/self-rate-limit wait must be measured and reported SEPARATELY from true model/API latency (methodology fix from the prior round).
